walkthroughs.h2: The brain of a smart product
walkthroughs.body_html: A microcontroller like the Arduino Uno or Raspberry Pi Pico reads inputs, runs code and switches outputs. Designers prototype with a USB cable and free software, then transfer the chip into a final PCB.
Common inputs include the LDR (light), thermistor (temperature), push button (user press) and PIR (motion). The chip reads them as voltages on its analogue or digital pins.

An LDR detects darkness, the microcontroller checks the value, and if dark it switches on a white LED output. Add a buzzer and you have a doorbell with night mode — all from the same three-block model.
